- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-horizon, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias starting from 3rd–5th day of forecast.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75% from prior peak) are common; cap forecast at +5–10% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 2–5%.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast instability; if sentiment shifts >0.3 in 2–3 days, reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing filter.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric correction: +3% bias early, -3% bias late if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., >5% in 1–2 days), model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 day lag correction to prevent premature peak.
